known_limitations_to_disclose: EXT_SOURCE values are anonymised Home Credit scores, not Equifax scores. Equifax bands are an approximate translation.
Amounts are in dataset currency units, not AUD. The assumed interest rate is illustrative.
AMT_GOODS_PRICE has a risk spike at exactly 450,000 (one loan product, about 20,800 training rows at 13.7% default).
ANNUITY_CREDIT has a risk spike for repayment-to-loan ratios of 0.0466 to 0.0497 (one loan product, 14.7% default). With the assumed rate, a 24-month term lands here.
The target is a payment-difficulty proxy, not a Basel 90+ DPD default. Output is an estimated probability of payment difficulty.

Pensioner, Unemployed, Businessman and Maternity leave applicants are out of policy and not scored. The model was trained including them (pensioners were 18% of rows at 5.4% default), so average PDs for the in-policy population may be slightly understated. Ranking is unaffected.
Trained on Home Credit applicants aged 20 to 69. Illustrative portfolio model, not a production lending model.
Fix for both spikes: monotonic binning constraint, planned for notebook 03.
Area rating uses the dataset's anonymised 1 to 3 region rating. A real lender would assign it from the postcode using an internal rating.

'Other business or industry (not listed)' uses the most common organisation band (8-10%). The anonymised industry, trade and transport types it covers actually range from under 6% to over 10% default, so their PDs are approximated.

The model uses three external credit scores; the form asks for one band and applies it to all three. Real applicants' three scores differ, so this shows how the model responds to a consistent credit profile.
